headline: DOE Has Not Fully Used Overseas Nuclear-Cleanup Lessons, GAO Says
dek: Auditors said British and Canadian approaches cut costs or decades from cleanup schedules while U.S. headquarters mostly treated international work as a teaching mission.

sources.title: Nuclear Waste Cleanup: DOE Is Missing Opportunities to Apply Lessons from Other Countries That Could Reduce Risks and Costs

lead.creator: Carlsbad Department of Development
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 license documented and reviewed on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.attribution: Carlsbad Department of Development / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
lead.caption: An underground salt bed at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant in New Mexico. GAO compared international nuclear-waste practices with the U.S. cleanup mission.
lead.alt: A worker and industrial equipment stand in a broad underground salt chamber used for nuclear waste disposal.

charts.caption: DOE estimates its environmental cleanup mission could cost $641 billion to $840 billion and continue until 2100.
charts.alt: Graphic shows a 641 to 840 billion dollar estimated U.S. cleanup cost and a timeline extending to 2100.

charts.caption: GAO highlighted at least £2 billion in UK savings and a Canadian plan expected to finish one priority cleanup nearly 30 years earlier.
charts.alt: Graphic lists at least 2 billion pounds in UK savings and nearly 30 years accelerated at one Canadian site.

paragraphs: The Energy Department is missing opportunities to apply nuclear-cleanup methods that other countries used to reduce costs, risks or schedules, the Government Accountability Office said in a July 29 report.

DOE's Office of Environmental Management is responsible for 15 U.S. sites contaminated by nuclear-weapons production and energy research. The office estimates that completing the mission could cost $641 billion to $840 billion and take until 2100.

GAO reviewed approaches in Belgium, Canada, France, Germany, Japan and the United Kingdom. The comparisons were intended to identify practices worth evaluating, not to claim that foreign sites and U.S. facilities are interchangeable.

The United Kingdom used a risk-informed approach that reduced the volume of low-radioactivity waste requiring repository disposal. GAO said the change produced at least £2 billion in savings, equivalent to about $2.6 billion in March 2026.

Canada prioritized cleanup at selected waste sites and expects one of those projects to finish nearly 30 years earlier. The report also described international work on waste sorting, reuse and treatment technologies.

Site officials told GAO they wanted more opportunities to learn from foreign counterparts. Headquarters officials said their international engagement typically focuses on teaching other countries rather than systematically gathering alternatives for U.S. decisions.

GAO recommended that DOE strategically engage partner countries, evaluate potentially useful approaches and periodically distribute the findings to site managers and other decision-makers. DOE agreed with the recommendation.

The cited foreign results do not establish that identical savings or schedule gains are available at U.S. sites. Geology, waste types, laws, contracts and community agreements differ, and each approach would require technical and regulatory review.

The oversight finding is therefore about the decision process: GAO concluded that a cleanup program measured in decades and hundreds of billions of dollars lacks a consistent system for testing relevant lessons already demonstrated abroad.
facts: DOE's cleanup mission covers 15 sites.
DOE estimates the mission could cost $641 billion to $840 billion and continue until 2100.
GAO reviewed six countries.
GAO cited at least £2 billion in UK savings.
Canada expects one priority cleanup to finish nearly 30 years earlier.
DOE agreed with GAO's recommendation.
uncertainty: Foreign results cannot be transferred directly to U.S. sites without technical, legal and site-specific evaluation.
DOE's cost range and completion date are estimates, not fixed outcomes.
seoTitle: GAO says DOE is missing overseas nuclear-cleanup lessons
seoDescription: GAO says DOE has not systematically applied foreign nuclear-cleanup lessons even as its U.S. mission could cost $641 billion to $840 billion.

headline: Justice Department Inventory Identifies 62 Criminal Regulatory Offenses
dek: The department also set out four factors prosecutors should generally weigh when regulatory violations can carry criminal penalties.
entities: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives

sources.title: Department of Justice Report: Criminal Regulatory Offenses
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Legal Policy

lead.creator: APK
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington. DOJ cataloged criminal regulatory offenses it can enforce and summarized its prosecution policy.
lead.alt: The long stone facade of the U.S. Justice Department headquarters fills a city block in Washington.

charts.caption: DOJ reported 62 criminal regulatory offenses and cataloged the available penalties and applicable intent standards.
charts.alt: Graphic shows 62 criminal regulatory offenses with penalties and intent standards cataloged.

charts.caption: The department's general policy names harm, potential gain, specialized expertise and awareness of unlawfulness among the factors prosecutors should consider.
charts.alt: Graphic lists four Justice Department prosecution factors: harm, gain, expertise and awareness.

paragraphs: The Justice Department identified 62 criminal regulatory offenses that it can enforce and cataloged their potential penalties and intent standards in an April 28 report to the Office of Management and Budget.

The inventory responds to Executive Order 14294, which directed executive agencies to list regulatory violations carrying criminal consequences. DOJ's Office of Legal Policy also distributed guidance and a model spreadsheet so agencies would report offenses in a consistent format.

DOJ said it is not a typical regulatory agency because it usually prosecutes criminal statutes enacted by Congress rather than creating offenses through its own rules. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives identified possible regulatory offenses for the department's list.

The report also states a general prosecution policy, subject to legal requirements and appropriate exceptions. Prosecutors should consider the harm or risk of harm associated with the alleged offense and the potential gain to the person under investigation.

Two other listed factors concern notice and expertise: whether a person held specialized knowledge or a relevant license, and evidence about awareness that the conduct was unlawful or knowledge of the specific regulation.

Those considerations are not a new element of every offense and do not guarantee a charging result. Statutes, regulations, department policy, admissible evidence and the facts of an individual matter still control prosecutorial decisions.

DOJ directed components to prioritize offenses that the department had enforced, threatened to enforce or expected to enforce. The resulting count should not be read as the total number of federal crimes or as a count of prosecutions.

The executive order cited more than 48,000 sections and 175,000 pages in the Code of Federal Regulations. Those figures describe the broader regulatory code; DOJ reported 62 offenses in its own inventory.

The report is a transparency record rather than a change to criminal liability by itself. Its practical effect is to make the department's identified regulatory offenses, penalty ranges and stated charging considerations easier to audit.
facts: DOJ identified 62 criminal regulatory offenses.
The report is dated April 28, 2026.
The inventory includes potential penalty ranges and applicable mens rea standards.
DOJ distributed standardized reporting guidance to executive agencies.
The prosecution policy lists four broad considerations.
uncertainty: The inventory is not a count of all federal crimes or of actual prosecutions.
The listed prosecution considerations do not determine an outcome in any individual case and are subject to law and policy exceptions.
seoTitle: DOJ inventory lists 62 criminal regulatory offenses
seoDescription: A Justice Department report identifies 62 criminal regulatory offenses and four broad factors for regulatory prosecution decisions.

headline: Smithsonian Program Will Mark Princess Grace's Legacy With Four Swan Benches
dek: The Sept. 1 event pairs a cultural-history program with permanent National Mall tributes during anniversaries of her royal marriage and Monaco's U.S. embassy.

sources.title: Smithsonian Associates Explores the Enduring Legacy of Princess Grace of Monaco

lead.creator: AgnosticPreachersKid
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: The Smithsonian Arts and Industries Building on the National Mall will host a Sept. 1 program examining the cultural legacy of Grace Kelly, Princess of Monaco.
lead.alt: The red-brick and stone Smithsonian Arts and Industries Building stands behind trees and a broad lawn.

charts.caption: The free, sold-out Sept. 1 program will combine a historian's presentation, an expert conversation and a reception at the Arts and Industries Building.
charts.alt: Graphic shows a September 1 Smithsonian program with history, expert discussion and a reception.

charts.caption: Four reproduced swan benches and Princess Grace roses will mark the 70th anniversary of her marriage and 20 years of Monaco's U.S. embassy.
charts.alt: Graphic lists four swan benches, a 70th royal-marriage anniversary and a 20th embassy anniversary.

paragraphs: Smithsonian Associates will examine the cultural legacy of Grace Kelly, Princess of Monaco, in a Sept. 1 program that also dedicates four reproduced swan benches as permanent tributes on the National Mall.

The free evening event at the Smithsonian's Arts and Industries Building is sold out, with a wait list available through Smithsonian Associates. It is organized with Smithsonian Gardens and the Embassy of Monaco.

A ceremony for invited guests will dedicate the benches in the Kathrine Dulin Folger Rose Garden. One bench will honor Princess Grace, and Princess Grace roses planted nearby are intended as a living public memorial.
The public program will include a historian's presentation about her life, support for the performing arts and Hollywood career, followed by a conversation among subject specialists and a reception.

A display inspired by the film 'To Catch a Thief' will accompany the reception. The program will also describe the Princess Grace Foundation-USA's support for early-career artists in theater, dance and film.
Kelly married Prince Rainier III in 1956. The event coincides with the 70th anniversary of that marriage and the 20th anniversary of Monaco establishing its embassy in Washington.

Smithsonian Associates placed the program in its Enduring Power of International Exchange series, which uses cultural programs to examine relationships between the United States and diplomatic partners.

The announcement calls the benches permanent, but it does not assign a monetary value to the installation or provide a future maintenance schedule. The program's public attendance is also constrained by the sold-out registration.

The durable public change is the garden tribute; the Sept. 1 discussion is a one-evening interpretation of how a U.S.-born actor became a symbol connecting film, philanthropy, the performing arts and Monaco-American exchange.
facts: The program is scheduled for Sept. 1 at 6:30 p.m.
The free event is sold out and has a wait list.
Four reproductions of a historic swan bench will be dedicated.
The program marks the 70th anniversary of Grace Kelly's marriage to Prince Rainier III.
It also marks 20 years since Monaco established its U.S. embassy.
uncertainty: The release does not provide a valuation or maintenance schedule for the permanent garden installations.
Wait-list availability does not guarantee admission to the sold-out event.
seoTitle: Smithsonian plans Princess Grace program and swan benches
seoDescription: A Sept. 1 Smithsonian program will examine Princess Grace's legacy and dedicate four swan benches on the National Mall.

headline: NIH Consortium Builds First Broad Atlas of Senescent Cells
dek: The SenNet papers introduce 'senotypes' to distinguish rare cells by tissue and condition, a step toward studying harmful and beneficial roles without treating them as one group.

sources.title: NIH research establishes new framework for the role of senescence in aging

lead.creator: Rhoda Baer / National Cancer Institute
lead.rightsBasis: National Cancer Institute photograph released into the public domain by the photographer and documented as an NIH work on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: Researchers work at a microscope in a National Cancer Institute laboratory. NIH's SenNet consortium is mapping rare senescent cells across human tissues and conditions.
lead.alt: One researcher looks through a microscope while a second researcher observes beside her in a laboratory.

charts.caption: SenNet is mapping senescent cells in tissues including the brain prefrontal cortex, lungs and lymph nodes using single-cell, spatial and computational methods.
charts.alt: Graphic lists brain, lung and lymph-node tissues alongside single-cell, spatial and AI methods.

charts.caption: The new 'senotype' framework groups senescent cells by tissue and surrounding conditions rather than treating cellular senescence as one uniform state.
charts.alt: Graphic shows senescent cells classified by tissue, health status and local environment.

paragraphs: An NIH-funded consortium has published the first broad atlas of senescent cells across human tissues and introduced a classification framework for cells that stop dividing but remain biologically active.

The Cellular Senescence Network, or SenNet, presented the work in a group of papers published June 11 in Cell. NIH launched the Common Fund program in 2021 because senescent cells are rare, diverse and difficult to identify in complex tissue.

Senescent cells are not uniformly harmful. They can support wound healing and help suppress tumors, while cells that accumulate with age can release inflammatory signals associated with chronic disease and other age-related changes.

The researchers call their new groupings 'senotypes.' The framework distinguishes cells according to tissue, health status and surrounding conditions, with the aim of preserving useful functions while identifying harmful subtypes for further study.

The atlas includes tissue maps from the brain's prefrontal cortex, lungs and lymph nodes. Consortium teams combined single-cell measurements, spatial methods, computational tools and artificial intelligence to detect cellular features.

NIH also reported blood markers associated in aging studies with kidney disease, frailty and future diabetes risk. Those research associations are not a clinical test recommendation and do not establish that the markers cause those outcomes.

The program is exploring experimental senolytics, drugs intended to remove selected senescent cells. The atlas is foundational research, however; it does not show that an approved therapy can safely target a senotype in patients.

Because the atlas spans multiple teams, tissues and measurement methods, definitions and validation will matter as the resource grows. A cell classified in one experimental setting may require confirmation in other populations and laboratories.

The immediate advance is a public research framework: scientists can ask where distinct senescent states occur and how they differ instead of relying on a single marker or assuming every nondividing cell has the same role.
facts: NIH launched SenNet in 2021.
The consortium published a compendium of papers in Cell on June 11, 2026.
The work introduces a classification concept called senotypes.
Mapped tissues include prefrontal cortex, lungs and lymph nodes.
The project uses single-cell, spatial, computational and AI-based methods.
uncertainty: The atlas is foundational research and does not establish an approved treatment or clinical screening test.
Biomarker associations require validation and do not by themselves show causation.
seoTitle: NIH SenNet atlas maps senescent cells by 'senotype'
seoDescription: NIH's SenNet consortium published a broad atlas of senescent cells and a 'senotype' framework for tissue-specific aging research.

headline: Wichita Will Join Dayton for Expanded March Madness Opening Round
dek: Both cities will host Tuesday-Wednesday tripleheaders in 2027 and 2028 after the NCAA enlarged the men's tournament field from 68 to 76 teams.
entities: Division I Men's Basketball Oversight Committee

sources.title: Wichita to serve as 2027 and 2028 Opening Round host for March Madness

lead.creator: Nnez9009
lead.rightsBasis: The photographer released the work into the public domain on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.caption: INTRUST Bank Arena in Wichita at night. The NCAA selected Wichita to join Dayton as an opening-round host for the 2027 and 2028 men's basketball tournaments.
lead.alt: A brightly lit indoor arena with a curved glass entrance stands against the night sky in Wichita.

charts.caption: Wichita and Dayton will each host three games Tuesday and three Wednesday after Selection Sunday in 2027 and 2028.
charts.alt: Graphic shows Wichita and Dayton each hosting three Tuesday games and three Wednesday games.

charts.caption: The Division I men's tournament is expanding from 68 to 76 teams, creating 12 opening-round games across the two cities.
charts.alt: Graphic shows the men's tournament growing from 68 to 76 teams with 12 opening-round games.

paragraphs: Wichita will join Dayton as an opening-round host for the 2027 and 2028 Division I men's basketball tournaments after the NCAA expanded the championship field from 68 to 76 teams.

Each city will stage three games on the Tuesday and three on the Wednesday after Selection Sunday. Across Wichita and Dayton, that produces 12 opening-round games over two days before the 64-team bracket continues.
Dayton has hosted the start of the men's tournament since 2001. The Wichita award adds a second opening-round site rather than replacing Dayton's long-running role.
The Division I Men's Basketball Committee selected Wichita from several interested cities. The Men's Basketball Oversight Committee approved the recommendation on July 9.
The NCAA announcement identifies Wichita as host for two tournament years. It does not establish a permanent second site beyond 2028, and later host selections remain separate decisions.

The expansion changes the entry path for more teams and adds inventory for venues and broadcasters. It also creates travel and scheduling questions that the full selection, seeding and bracketing procedures will need to address.

The NCAA said the complete principles and procedures for the 2027 championship would be posted later in the summer. Until then, the host and game counts are final while some bracket mechanics remain forthcoming.
A larger field does not guarantee a particular conference or team more bids. At-large and automatic qualification decisions will still be made under the championship's adopted selection procedures.
For Wichita, the concrete award is six opening-round games in each of 2027 and 2028. For viewers, the first visible structural change is that March Madness will begin simultaneously in two cities.
facts: The men's tournament field is expanding from 68 to 76 teams.
Wichita will host opening-round games in 2027 and 2028.
Dayton will remain an opening-round host.
Each city will host three games Tuesday and three Wednesday.
The Oversight Committee approved Wichita on July 9, 2026.
uncertainty: The Wichita award covers 2027 and 2028 and does not establish the host arrangement beyond those years.
The NCAA had not yet posted the full 2027 selection, seeding and bracketing procedures in the cited announcement.
seoTitle: Wichita joins Dayton for expanded March Madness opening round
seoDescription: Wichita will host 2027 and 2028 March Madness opening-round games as the men's NCAA field expands from 68 to 76 teams.

headline: IMF Cuts Austria's 2026 Growth Outlook to 0.6% as Energy Prices Rise
dek: The fund projects 3.2% inflation this year and says additional fiscal measures may be needed to reach Austria's 3% deficit target in 2028.

sources.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation with Austria

lead.creator: Fabian Lackner
lead.rightsBasis: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 license granted by the photographer on Wikimedia Commons.
lead.attribution: Fabian Lackner / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
lead.caption: Vienna's skyline across the Danube. The IMF expects Austria's recovery to continue in 2026 but at a slower 0.6% pace.
lead.alt: Vienna's modern skyline reflects in calm water beneath a pale winter sky.

charts.caption: The IMF projects Austria's real GDP growth at 0.6% and average inflation at 3.2% in 2026.
charts.alt: Graphic shows Austria's 2026 growth forecast of 0.6 percent and inflation forecast of 3.2 percent.

charts.caption: Austria targets a 3% deficit in 2028, while the IMF estimates potential growth will ease toward 0.8% by 2031 without stronger productivity.
charts.alt: Graphic shows a 3 percent deficit target for 2028 and 0.8 percent potential growth by 2031.

paragraphs: Austria's economy is expected to grow 0.6% in 2026 as higher energy prices weigh on household consumption, the International Monetary Fund said after its annual policy review.
The country emerged from a two-year recession with 1.0% growth in 2025. The IMF expects the recovery to continue, but more slowly than before the latest energy-price shock.

Headline inflation reached 3.8% in May after gasoline pump prices rose roughly 20% from a year earlier. The fund projects inflation averaging 3.2% in 2026 before gradually moving toward the euro-area average.

The IMF expects stronger growth in 2028 and 2029 as inflation moderates and household saving patterns normalize. It then sees potential growth easing toward about 0.8% by 2031, below the previous decade's 1.2% average.
Austria's deficit reached 4.6% of GDP in 2024, leading to an EU excessive-deficit procedure. The government aims to bring the deficit to 3% in 2028.

The fund called that target appropriately ambitious but said the announced measures may not be sufficient. Backward-looking indexation of wages and social benefits has made near-term consolidation more gradual.

IMF directors emphasized productivity reforms, labor supply and careful sequencing of fiscal measures. Austria's shrinking workforce and weak productivity growth are central constraints in the medium-term outlook.

The forecast is conditional, not a guaranteed result. Energy supply disruptions, external competition and wider geopolitical developments could weaken growth or keep inflation higher, while stronger investment or productivity could improve the path.

The Article IV assessment therefore describes a narrow recovery with limited room for error: positive growth continues, but energy costs, fiscal adjustment and slow productivity leave Austria below its recent potential.
facts: The IMF projects 0.6% Austrian GDP growth in 2026.
Austria grew 1.0% in 2025 after a two-year recession.
The IMF projects 3.2% inflation in 2026.
Austria targets a 3% deficit in 2028.
The IMF estimates potential growth around 0.8% by 2031.
uncertainty: The forecast is sensitive to energy prices, geopolitical developments and external demand.
The IMF said additional fiscal consolidation may be needed but did not prescribe a single guaranteed policy path.
seoTitle: IMF projects 0.6% growth for Austria in 2026
seoDescription: The IMF expects Austria to grow 0.6% with 3.2% inflation in 2026 and says its 2028 deficit target may require more measures.
